  {"step": 3, "file": "src/flb_http_client.c", "function": "proxy_parse", "line": 449, "var": "proxy", "code": "if (strncmp(proxy, \"http://\", 7) == 0) {...} else if (strncmp(proxy, \"https://\", 8) == 0) {...} else { return -1; }", "note": "The proxy string starts with 'A' (0x41), not 'http://' or 'https://', so proxy_parse returns -1 (parse failure)."},
  {"step": 4, "file": "src/flb_http_client.c", "function": "flb_http_client", "line": 719, "var": "buf", "code": "if (ret != 0) { flb_free(buf); flb_http_client_destroy(c); return NULL; }", "note": "On proxy parse failure, flb_free(buf) frees the header buffer that c->header_buf already points to."},
  {"step": 5, "file": "src/flb_http_client.c", "function": "flb_http_client_destroy", "line": 777, "var": "c->header_buf", "code": "flb_free(c->header_buf);", "note": "flb_http_client_destroy frees c->header_buf, which aliases the already-freed buf, causing a heap double-free."}
]
EOF

4. Then `flb_http_client_destroy(c)` is called, which frees `c->header_buf` (same pointer as buf) again → double-free.
